title: Determining Cage-Escape Yields Using Nanosecond Transient Absorption Spectroscopy
author: Ripak, De Kreijger, et al.

steps.title: Prepare photosensitizer stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve the photosensitizer ([Ru(bpy)₃]²⁺) in acetonitrile to obtain a solution whose absorbance at the excitation wavelength (λ_exc) is between 0.3 and 0.6. Prepare 6 mL if you will use a single cuvette for all data points, or 20 mL if you will use five individual cuvettes.

steps.title: Prepare reference actinometer
steps.instruction: Make 3 mL of a reference actinometer solution using the prototypical [Ru(bpy)₃]²⁺ in acetonitrile, adjusting the concentration so that its absorbance at λ_exc is also between 0.3 and 0.6.

steps.title: Prepare quencher solution
steps.instruction: Weigh the quencher (4‑methoxy‑benzene diazonium tetrafluoroborate) and dissolve it in 2 mL or 4 mL of the photosensitizer stock to give a 20 mM quencher solution. Prepare this solution immediately before the experiment; if it must be stored, keep it at 4 °C in the dark. The quencher is added to the PS stock to avoid dilution‑induced changes in absorbance during titration.

steps.title: Measure absorption changes
steps.instruction: For each quencher concentration, record the change in absorbance of the oxidized photosensitizer (ΔA_PS⁺) and the change in absorbance of the excited‑state reference (ΔA_ESref) at their respective detection wavelengths, as well as the absorbances of the reference and PS solutions at λ_exc (Abs_ref(λ_exc) and Abs_PS(λ_exc)).

steps.title: Calculate relative PS⁺ yield (Φ)
steps.instruction:
Use Equation 5 to compute the relative yield of PS⁺ for each quencher concentration:
Φ = (ΔA_PS⁺/Δε_PS⁺ + ΔA_ESref/Δε_ESref) × (1 − 10^{‑Abs_ref(λ_exc)}) / (1 − 10^{‑Abs_PS(λ_exc)})².
Insert the Δε values determined by photolysis: Δε₍actinometer₎ = ‑11000 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹ at 450 nm and Δε₍[Ru(bpy)₃]³⁺/²⁺₎ = ‑9000 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹ at 450 nm.

steps.title: Determine % photoluminescence quenched
steps.instruction: Measure the steady‑state or time‑resolved photoluminescence of the photosensitizer in the presence of each quencher concentration and calculate the percentage of quenched photoluminescence (% PL quenched).

steps.title: Plot Φ versus % PL quenched
steps.instruction: Create a plot of the calculated Φ values (from step 4) against the corresponding % PL quenched values (from step 5). Use the data shown in Table 1 as a representative example:

substeps.instruction: Δε_PS⁺ at λ_det: –9000 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹ (all points)
Δε_ESref at 450 nm: –11000 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹ (all points)

steps.title: Calculate cage‑escape yield (Φ_CE)
steps.instruction: Perform a linear regression of Φ versus % PL quenched constrained to pass through the origin. The slope of this regression equals the cage‑escape yield (Φ_CE). Report the regression statistics (R² ≈ 95 % for steady‑state data, ≈ 90 % for time‑resolved data) and the resulting yields (≈ 34 % from steady‑state, ≈ 32 % from time‑resolved measurements). An estimated experimental error of ~10 % should be noted.
